tei:titleStmt.tei:title: סדר תפילת השיר
Seder Tefilat haShir — the recitation of the Songs of Ascents before Shabbat and Festival services, as found in Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba and Minhag Kaffa

tei:div.tei:head: Seder Tefilat haShir — the recitation of the Songs of Ascents before Shabbat and Festival services, as found in Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba and Minhag Kaffa

tei:l.tei:note: The elaborate introduction to the cycle found in the Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba:

tei:lg.tei:l: And these are the last words of David!
Quoth David son of Jesse,
and quoth the man raised on high,
anointed by Jacob’s God,
and sweet singer of Israel. (II Samuel 23:1)
Allow me to sweetly sing to the Noble and Awesome
By whose word all was created.
Great are You, and great is Your name in might! (Jeremiah 10:6)
Dicta of Yours stand in heaven, high and awesome!
Ever-knowing Witness! Who says “my path is hidden”
when You are the Sole God of forgiving, strong in atoning?
Zero out our willful sins in our straying; atone for the wayward!
Have mercy and compassion on the people lifted by wings!
To be a refuge on a stressful day, the Cause is good. (Naḥum 1:7)
Yah! Save us from wrath and rage!
Compile the exiles of the scattered sheep.
Look to Your name, great, mighty, awesomeDeity,
Majestic and awesome Sovereign!
Notice our groaning, Girt in Might!
Splatter our adversaries and foes in ire and fury!
O Terrific and Awesome, we stand before You in pleas.
Face us, for we are wrapped up in stress!
Charged with Your name are we, o Rock.
Quicken our fate and salvation to enlighten!
Remove us, Lofty One, from darkness to light!
Sheltering in the auratic heavens, the Surveyor with whom light abides.
Show heed to the song-singers’s cry and praise from the created people’s mouth.
Thanks, praise, and the sound of song will burst from our lips.
As it is written:
Thus my lips will burst with praise,
for You taught me Your laws.
Thoughts of You will my tongue call,
for all Your commandments are justice.
That Your hand be my help!
For Your testimonies I chose.
Thirsting am I for Your salvation, Cause,
and Your teaching is my delight.
That my soul live and praise You,
and You justice help me!
Though like a lost sheep I strayed,
search out Your servant,
for Your commandments I have not forgotten. (Psalms 119:171–176)
To tell in the morning Your mercy,
and Your faithfulness at night. (Psalms 92:3)
O Cause, in the morning hear my voice,
in the morning I set before You and wait. (Psalms 5:4)
And I cry out to You, Cause,
and in the morning my prayer goes before You. (Psalms 88:14)
And my tongue pronounces Your justice,
all day Your praise. (Psalms 35:28)
Let me sing, please, of my beloved,
a song of my beloved, for his vineyard;
a vineyard my beloved had on the rich hill. (Isaiah 5:1)
On that day will this song be sung in the land of Judah:
a strong city is ours! Salvation set, walls and forts. (Isaiah 26:1)
The song of songs that is Solomon’s. (Song of Songs 1:1)
And as for me, I sing Your strength,
and I cheer for the morning Your mercy,
for You were my refuge and shelter
on a stressful day of mine. (Psalms 59:17)

tei:l.tei:note: The catena introduction found in Minhag Kaffa:

tei:lg.tei:l: And these are the last words of David!
Quoth David son of Jesse,
and quoth the man raised on high,
anointed by Jacob’s God,
and sweet singer of Israel.
The Cause’s spirit spoke in me,
and Their word on my tongue. (II Samuel 23:1–2)
And as for me, I sing Your strength,
and I cheer for the morning Your mercy,
for You were my refuge and shelter
on a stressful day of mine. (Psalms 59:17)
In my stress I call to the Cause,
and to my God I cry;
They hear my voice from Their palace,
and my cry before Them comes
into Their ears. (Psalms 18:7)
The Cause to save me,
and my harmonies we will harmonize
all the days of our lives
to the house of the Cause. (Isaiah 38:20)
Hear, kings;
give ear, princes!
As for me, to the Cause,
as for me, let me sing,
I will hymn to the Cause, God of Israel. (Judges 5:3)
A song of ascents.
To the Cause in the strife I faced,
I called and They answered.
Cause, redeem my being
from lying lips,
from slippery tongue!
What can you get,
what can you gain,
o slippery tongue?
Warrior’s arrows, sharpened,
hot coals of bramble.
Woe is me, for I dwell in Meshekh,
that I live with the nomads’ tents!
So long I myself have lived here,
with those who hate peace.
I am “Peace!” but as I speak,
they are for war.
And a spirit enwrapped Amashai, head of the adjutants:
“To you, David, and to your people, Jesses’s on, peace!
Peace to you, and peace to your Helper,
for your God helped you!”
And David welcomed them
and set them at the head of the troop. (I Chronicles 12:19)
Creator of the speech of lips —
peace, peace to the near and far! —
said the Cause —
and I will heal him. (Isaiah 57:19)
A song for ascents.
I lift my eyes to the mountains —
from where will my help come?
My help is from with the Cause, Maker of heaven and earth.
They will not let your foot slip;
your Guardian does not slumber.
Hey, neither slumbering nor sleeping is Israel’s Guardian!
The Cause is your guardian,
the Cause is the shade on your right hand.
By day the sun will not strike you,
nor the moon by night.
The Cause will guard you from all evil,
will guard your life.
The Cause will guard your goings and comings
from now and forevermore.
And at the end of days
will the mountain of the house of the Cause
be properly at the head of mountains,
and raised over hills,
and all the nations will stream towards it.
And many peoples will walk and say,
“Let’s go ascend to the mountain of the Cause,
to the house of Jacob’s God,
and we wil learn from Their ways
and walk in Their paths!”
For from Zion will come teaching,
and the word of the Cause from Jerusalem. (Isaiah 2:2–3)
A song of ascents, David’s.
I rejoiced when they said to me,
“To the house of the Cause we go up!”
Our feet were standing in your gates, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, built up like a city knit together.
For there the tribes ascended;
the tribes of Yah, witnesses for Israel
to give thanks to the name of the Cause.
For there sat the thrones of judgement,
the thrones of the house of David.
Seek the peace of Jerusalem;
may those who love you be at peace.
May there be peace within your walls,
prosperity in your palaces.
For the sake of my siblings and comrades,
I wish to speak, please, of your peace.
For the sake of the House of the Cause our God,
I request good for you.
For Mine are the children of Israel, servants,
My servants they are, whom I took from the land of Egypt;
I am the Cause your God. (Leviticus 25:55)
For My servants are they, whom I took from the land of Egypt;
not to be sold for a servant’s price. (Leviticus 25:42)
Let us search and investigate our ways
and return to the Cause.
Let us lift up our hearts in our palms
to the Deity in heaven. (Lamentations 3:40–41)
A song of ascents.
To You I raise my eyes, the Dweller in heaven.
Hey, like the eyes of servants to their masters’ hands,
like the eyes of a maid to her mistress’s hand,
thus our eyes are to the Cause our God
until They grace us.
Grace us, Cause, grace us,
for we are so sated with contempt.
Greatly sated are our souls
with the mocking of the complacent,
the contempt of the arrogant-oppressors.
Were it not for the God of my father,
the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, being mine,
you would have now sent me off empty!
My poverty and the toil of my hands
God saw and decided last night. (Genesis 31:42)
A song of ascents, David’s.
Were it not for the Cause who has been ours —
Israel should say —
were it not for the Cause who has been ours when a mortal rises against us,
then we would have been swallowed alive in their furious rage at us;
then the water would have swept us away, the torrent would pass over our necks,
then the raging waters would pass over our necks.
Blessed be the Cause who did not give us to be prey to their teeth.
Our neck is like a bird escaping from a fowler’s trap, the trap shattered, we escaped.
Our help is in the name of the Cause, Maker of heaven and earth.
Blessed be the man who trusts in the Cause,
and for whom the Cause is his trust. (Jeremiah 17:7)
Trust in the Cause forever and aye,
for in Yah the Cause is the rock of eternities. (Isaiah 26:4)
And those who know Your name trust in You,
for You have not abandoned those who seek You out, Cause. (Psalms 9:11)
A song of ascents.
Those trusting in the Cause are like Mount Zion,
unshaking, forever dwelling.
Jerusalem, mountains surround her;
and the Cause surrounds Their people
from now and forevermore.
For the staff of the wicked will never rest on the lot of the righteous —
in that the righteous not set their hands to iniquity.
Do good, Cause, to the good, and the upright-hearted.
But the bent in their crookedness,
the Cause will lead them by their wicked deeds;
peace upon Israel!
Thus I may turn My hand towards you
and clean your scum with lye,
so I may remove your waste.
Thus I may return your judges as of old
and your advisors as of yore,
and after that you will be called the Righteous City,
the Faithful Town!
Zion in judgement will be saved,
and returned in righteousness! (Isaiah 1:25–27)
A song of ascents.
When the Cause would return the returning of Zion
we would be like dreamers.
Thus full would be our mouths with laughter
and our tongues joy;
thus the nations will say,
“The Cause has done greatness with them!”
The Cause has done greatness with us,
we would be happy.
Return, Cause, our returning,
like arroyos in the desert.
Those who sow in tears
will reap in joy.
One going out weeping,
carrying a seed-bag
will come in cheer
carrying his sheaves.
Woe, one who builds his house unfairly,
his high chambers unjustly;
who works his fellow without pay,
and does not repay his labor! (Jeremiah 22:12)
Thus Solomon said,
“The Cause said to dwell in a cumulus.
Building I have built a glory-house for You,
a foundation of Your dwelling eternal.” (I Kings 8:12–13)
A song of ascents, Solomon’s.
If the Cause will not build a house,
vainly do its builders toil on it;
if the Cause will not guard a city,
vainly do its guards look out.
Vainly do you wake up early,
stay up late,
eating bread of sorrow;
as They give Their beloved sleep.
Hey, the Cause’s inheritence is children,
reward is the womb’s fruit.
Like arrows in the hand of the warrior
are children of youth.
Content is the man
who fills his quiver with them;
they will be unshamed when speaking
with the emenies in the gate.
Content is the mortal who listens to me,
to guard my gates day by day,
to guard the doorposts of my openings. (Proverbs 8:34)
Content is the human who does so,
the mortal child who holds strongly to it:
guarding the sabbath from its profanation,
his hand from doing any evil. (Isaiah 56:2)
A song of ascents.
Content are all those who revere the Cause,
who walk in Their ways.
Your handiwork you will consume,
you will be content and it will be good for you.
Your wife, like a fruitful vine in the recesses of your house;
your children like olive-plants around your table.
Hey, this is how a man reverent of the Cause is blessed.
May the Cause bless you from Zion!
And see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
And see children of your children —
peace upon Israel!
And I passed over you and saw you wallowing in your blood,
and I said to you, “By your blood you will live,”
and I said to you, “By your blood you will live.”
Increase like the vegetation of the field I gave you,
and you increased and grew and came decorated in decorations,
your breasts firmed and your hair grew,
though you were naked and bare. (Ezekiel 16:6–7)
A song of ascents.
Increasingly have they stressed me
since my youth —
Israel should say —
increasingly have they stressed me
since my youth,
yet they have not overcome me.
On my back ploughers have ploughed,
lengthening their furrows.
The Cause righteously snapped
the ropes of the wicked.
They should be ashamed, turned back,
all who hate Zion.
They should be like roof-grass,
which before it is pulled dries,
filling neither the harvester’s palm
nor the sheave-gatherer’s chest.
Let no passersby say
“the Cause’s blessing upon you!
We have blessed you in the Cause’s name!”
I called Your name, Cause,
from the lowest pits.
My voice You heard;
do not hide Your ear
from relieving my cry!
You came close on the day I called You;
saying “Do not fear.” (Lamentations 3:55–57)
A song of ascents.
From the depths I have called You, Cause.
Master, hear my voice,
may Your ears be inclined
to the sound of my petitions!
If You account for iniquities, Yah,
Master, who can stand?
For with You is forgiveness,
that You be revered.
I wait for the Cause,
my being awaits,
for Their word I have hoped.
My being is for the Master
as those watching for the morning
watch for the morning.
Israel, hope for the Cause,
for with the Cause is mercy
and great redemption.
And They will redeem Israel
from all its iniquities.
And the man Moses was very humble,
more than any mortal on the face of the earth. (Numbers 12:3)
Not so My servant Moses;
in all My house he is trusted. (Numbers 12:7)
A song of ascents, David’s.
O Cause,
my heart is not high,
nor my eyes lofty,
nor have I walked in what is too great and profound for me.
Haven’t I been calm and stilled my soul
like a toddler with his mother;
like a toddler upon me is my being!
Israel will await the Cause
from now and forevermore.
And now, rise, Cause God, to Your rest-place,
You and the ark of Your strength;
Your priests, Cause God, will wear salvation,
and Your pious ones will rejoice in good.
Cause God, do not turn back Your anointed one’s face;
remember the mercies of David Your servant. (II Chronicles 6:41–42)
A song of ascents.
Remember, Cause, David, all his self-affliction!
As he swore a vow to the Cause, to Jacob’s Might:
“I should not enter the tent of my house,
nor go up onto my bed-couch,
nor give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids;
until I find a place for the Cause, abodes for Jacob’s Might.”
Hey, we heard it by Ephrath,
we found it in the forest fields.
Let’s come to Their abodes,
let’s bow to Their footstool!
Rise, Cause, to Your resting-place,
You and the ark of Your strength;
Your priests will wear righteousness
and Your pious ones will cheer.
For the sake of David Your servant
do not turn back Your anointed one’s face.
The Cause swore to David truly, unrenounced:
“From the fruit of your womb I will set a throne for you.
If your children guard My covenant
and this testimony of Mine I teach them,
their children will forevermore sit on the throne for you.”
For the Cause chose Zion, desiring it as Their seat:
“This is My resting-place forevermore,
here I will sit for I desire it.
Its provisions I will bless, blessing;
its needy ones I will sate with bread.
And its priests I will clothe in salvation,
and its pious ones will cheer, cheering.
There I will sprout up a horn for David,
arranging a light for My anointed.
His enemies I will cloth in shame,
and on him his crown will shine.”
Good are two, more so than one,
for they have a good reqard for their labor. (Ecclesiastes 4:9)
And if one attacks, two can stand against it;
and the threefold cord is not quickly broken! (Ecclesiastes 4:12)
A song of ascents, David’s.
Hey, how good and how pleasant is it
when brothers dwell together!
Like good oil on the head,
descending down the beard, Aaron’s beard,
descending to the collar of his garb.
Like Hermon’s dew,
descending on the mountains of Zion,
for there the Cause commanded blessing,
life until eternity!
Come, bless the Cause your God,
from eternity to eternity!
And may Your glorious name be blessed and exalted
over all blessing and praise. (Nehemiah 9:5)
A song of ascents.
Hey, bless the Cause,
all servants of the Cause,
standing in the house of the Cause nightly.
Raise your hands in holiness
and bless the Cause.
The Cause, Maker of heaven and earth,
will bless you from Zion.

tei:l.tei:note: These final two psalms and their catenae are only found in the Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba:

tei:lg.tei:l: Praise Yah!
Praise the name of the Cause!
Praise, servants of the Cause,
who stand in the Cause’s house;
in the courts of our God’s house!
Praise Yah, for the Cause is good;
hymn Their name for it is sweet!
For Yah chose Jacob for Themself;
Israel Their treasure.
For I know the Cause is great,
and our Master over all deities.
All that the Cause desires is done,
on heaven and on earth,
in the seas and all the abysses.
Raising clouds from the earth’s edge,
They made lightning for rain,
letting out wind from its vaults.
They smote the firstborn of Egypt,
from man to beast.
They sent signs and portents
into the midst of Egypt;
against Pharaoh and all his servants.
They smote great nations,
and killed mighty kings,
Siḥon king of Amurru,
and Og king of Bashan,
and all the kingdoms of Canaan,
and gave their land as inheritance,
inheritance for Israel Their people.
Cause, Your name is forever!
Cause, Your memory to each generation.
For the Cause will judge Their people
and avenge Their servants.
The nations’ idols are silver and gold,
the work of human hand.
Mouths they have but do not speak;
eyes they have but do not see;
ears they have but do not hear;
noses but no breath in them.
Like them will be their makers,
all who trust in them.
House of Israel, bless the Cause!
House of Aaron, bless the Cause!
House of Levi, bless the Cause!
God-fearers, bless the Cause!
Bless the Cause from Zion,
dwelling in Jerusalem.
Praise Yah!
Thus said the Deity Cause,
Creator of heaven and its expanse,
Stretcher of the earth and its produce,
granting breath to the people upon it,
and spirit to those walking upon it, (Isaiah 42:5)
Maker of light and Creator of dark,
Maker of peace and Creator of evil,
I the Cause do all this. (Isaiah 45:7)
Thank the Cause, who is good,
whose mercy is eternal!
Thank the God of gods,
whose mercy is eternal!
Thank the Master of masters,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who does great wonders alone,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who makes heaven in intelligence,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who stretches land on the water,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who makes great lights,
whose mercy is eternal!
The sun to rule the day,
whose mercy is eternal!
The moon and stars to rule by night,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who smites Egypt’s firstborn,
whose mercy is eternal!
and brings Israel from in it,
whose mercy is eternal!
with a strong hand and outstretched arm,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who splits the Reed Sea to splittings,
whose mercy is eternal!
to let Israel pass through it,
whose mercy is eternal!
And emptied Pharaoh and his forces in the Reed Sea,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who led Their people in the wilds,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who smote great kings,
whose mercy is eternal!
And killed mighty kings,
whose mercy is eternal!
Siḥon king of Amurru,
whose mercy is eternal!
and Og king of Bashan,
whose mercy is eternal!
And gave their land as inheritance,
whose mercy is eternal!
Inheritance for Israel Their servant,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who in our lowness remembered us,
whose mercy is eternal!
And saved us from our stresses,
whose mercy is eternal!
Who gives bread to all flesh,
whose mercy is eternal!
Thank the God of Heaven,
whose mercy is eternal!
For great is Their kindness over us,
and the truth of the Cause is forever.
Praise Yah! (Psalms 117:2)
And You are holy, seated on Israel’s praises.
In You our ancestors trusted,
they trusted and You rescued them.
To You they cried, and escaped;
in You they trusted and were unashamed. (Psalms 22:4–6)
And we are Your people
and the flock You shepherd;
we thank You forever,
from era to era we will tell Your praise. (Psalms 79:13)
Save, Cause, Your people, the remnant of Israel! (Jeremiah 31:6)
Save us, Cause our God,
and gather us from the nations,
to thank Your holy name
and laud Your praise.
Bless the Cause, God of Israel,
from eternity until eternity,
and all the people say amen,
praise Yah! (Psalms 106:47–48)
Bless the Cause forever,
amen and amen! (Psalms 89:53)

tei:note.tei:p: ”With whom light abides” is in Aramaic, a borrowing from Daniel 2:22
This verse only found in Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba.

Two notes: (1) from here on, the bolded Leitworte of the catena correspond to the following psalm rather than the previous. (2) These verses, as well as the entirely of Psalm 123, are entirely missing from the Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba.
This verse only found in Minhag Kaffa.
Just Isaiah 1:26–27 in Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba
This verse only found in Minhag Kaffa.
Only I Kings 8:13 found in Minhag Kaffa
“Me” in context is not God, but the personification of wisdom, and thus not capitalized.
Note that there is no Leitwort in common here, but rather a theme: humility.

Note that in Maḥzor Aram Ṣoba the first half of 6:41 is replaced with Psalm 132:8, but this is not included here, because it is likely a printer’s error, seeing as (1) nowhere else is a verse from the psalm in question found in the psalm’s respective catena, (2) Chronicles is an understudied book and it is very possible the editor didn’t recognize the text and “corrected” it to the more well-known verse in Psalms, and (3) the passage in Chronicles, a relatively late book, is likely a reference to this very psalm, being close enough in content that marking specific Leitworte would make almost the entire text bold.
